newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HOWE GIVING IT ANOTHER TRY, WITH SIOUX FALLS TEAM.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HOWE GIVING IT ANOTHER TRY, WITH SIOUX FALLS TEAM.

text.p: Former major league pitcher Steve Howe, suspended seven times during his career for drug and alcohol-related activity, is giving baseball another try after signing a contract Thursday with Sioux Falls of the Independent Northern League.

Howe, 39, last played for the New York Yankees, who released him last June 22. The next day he was arrested at New York's Kennedy Airport after police found a loaded .357-calibre Magnum in his carry-on luggage.
Howe was sentenced to three years' probation and 150 hours of community service after pleading guilty to a misdemeanor weapons possession charge.
Howe spent the last six years of his 12-year major league career with the Yankees. He has a career record of 47-41 with 91 saves and a 3.03 ERA in 497 major-league games.

Howe began his big league career with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1980 and captured National League Rookie of the Year honours. He was the closer on the Dodgers' 1981 World Series winners. Howe has also pitched for Minnesota and Texas.
